cases.claim: “Lewis is selecting produce” ... “brush[es] hands accidently” ... “really hitting it off” | “Lewis . . . at a wedding and heading to the dance floor” ... “[t]he woman from the grocery story is Lewis’ date!”
cases.context: Romantic story arc runs through frames 18–33 while the boxed warning (serious, life-threatening infections) is disclosed; multiple scene changes and background music.
cases.rationale: Compelling, attention-grabbing presentation with scene changes and music interferes with comprehension of the major statement.
cases.check: Storyboard check: flag narrative 'reveals', scene cuts, and music during boxed-warning audio; pairwise judge comprehension vs. a calmer variant.

cases.cat: Distracting presentation of material efficacy qualifier (SUPER)
cases.claim: VO: “It’s a twice-daily pill that substantially improved hemoglobin levels compared to SOLIRIS® or ULTOMIRIS® infusions” | graphic: “IMPROVED HEMOGLOBIN LEVELS COMPARED TO SOLIRIS® OR ULTOMIRIS® INFUSIONS”
cases.context: Qualifying SUPER (82% vs 0% with Hb increase; 68% vs 0% Hb levels without transfusion, 24-week study) shows 65 words in ~9 seconds (433 wpm) while a larger animated claim graphic and music compete.
cases.rationale: SUPER cannot be read/comprehended at that speed amid competing presentations; undermines material efficacy information.
cases.check: Rule: compute SUPER words-per-minute (words / on-screen seconds × 60); flag > ~238 wpm (FDA cites 175–300 range); flag when claim graphic is larger/more central than qualifying SUPER.
